pass_requires.about: What a PASS of this scenario must contain (v0.7.2 Phase 9): the gate refuses a PASS verdict with fewer checks or runs, without a named check, or with fewer checks of a family than the whole scenario makes. A check that is missing was not passed.

win32.pattern: ^(aqua geometry regression: native macOS metrics only|the aqua branch needs aqua)$
^(this (environment|account) (cannot create|may not create)|cannot make a symbolic link here$)
^Windows refused to create a real symbolic link \(WinError 1314: this account does not hold the symbolic\-link privilege, Developer Mode is off\), so the link rejection cannot be exercised here$
win32.why: v0.8.1 Checkpoint F2: test_optional_tts_setup.py::test_windows_keeps_its_strict_no_link_rule_and_never_reads_a_chain creates real symbolic links, which Windows allows only to an account with SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege or Developer Mode. The test skips on exactly OSError.winerror 1314 and re-raises every other error; it never simulates a link. The no-link rule's deterministic half (a real console Python accepted, a missing one refused, the POSIX rule never consulted) is the separate passing test_windows_accepts_a_real_console_python_and_refuses_a_missing_one. On an account with the privilege the test runs and this skip does not occur.

^got empty parameter set for

win32.pattern: ^(POSIX\ process\ groups\ \(Windows\ ends\ its\ Job\ Object\))$
win32.why: v0.8.x P5-A and P5-A-R1: test_optional_tts_setup.py's 18 tests of a POSIX setup worker's process group. P5-A's 7: it is never reaped before its group is ended (a valid result, a cancel it obeys, a crash, a worker reaped behind the run's back, bystanders, the client's loop, fail-closed start without the ownership module). P5-A-R1's 11: a run whose group was not confirmed empty is never a success (unproved by wait and by result(), remaining, signalled, an install success, no result, Cancel and time-out with unconfirmed cleanup, the client), and Cancel and time-out with confirmed cleanup keep their outcomes. Windows ends the same tree through its Job Object, pinned by the existing tree tests and by the cross-platform tests that a run with a job keeps the released path and the worker's own success.

win32.pattern: ^(POSIX\ first\-run\ ownership\ \(Windows\ ends\ its\ Job\ Object\))$
win32.why: v0.8.x P5-B: test_first_run_setup_ownership.py's 19 tests of the first-run window's POSIX ownership of its optional-setup workers (the owner and spawn path, a completed check and install, Cancel, closing the window and time-out during a blocked step, a worker leaving a probe and a child, settling after the window closes, an unconfirmed end, no start after close, SIGKILL, a crash, Force Quit, and the owner ending before, during and just after the worker). Windows' first-run window takes no new ownership (pinned by test_windows_first_run_window_takes_no_new_ownership, which runs everywhere) and ends the same tree through its Job Object, pinned by the existing tree tests. Nothing Windows ran before is skipped by this rule.

win32.pattern: ^(POSIX\ normal\-exit\ group\ retirement\ \(Windows:\ Job\ Objects\))$
win32.why: v0.8.x P5-C: test_normal_exit_group_retirement.py's 36 tests of POSIX process groups when a pip or probe exits normally: the follower that waits for the leader's exit (not its output), ends its group the P5-A way and reaps it last; the base install's pip, probes, -m venv and offline pip (Owner.run_python, its subprocess.run arguments and results, time-out, failure and crash); 'Stop setup?' never reaping pip; the optional-setup worker's run_command (helper on /dev/null or on pip's output, under an owner or in its own session, failure, crash, Cancel); a leader reaped behind its caller's back and an unconfirmed group end reported as failures; the orderly end checking and signalling only under the waitpid lock and racing a run's own retirement; end to end under the first-run window and the app window, and the real first-run window. Windows keeps its Job Object, taskkill /T and subprocess.run paths, pinned by test_windows_run_command_keeps_its_job_object_path and test_windows_base_install_keeps_its_released_spawn_paths, which run everywhere. Nothing Windows ran before is skipped by this rule.

win32.pattern: ^(POSIX\ synthesis\-worker\ group\ retirement\ \(Windows:\ Job\ Objects\))$
win32.why: v0.8.x P5-D: test_synthesis_worker_group_retirement.py's 26 tests of POSIX process groups when a synthesis worker ends: the local-engine worker (a crash with a helper on /dev/null, on its stderr or on its protocol channel; an engine-switch close; alive() never reaping; Cancel after an idle worker exited, through the run's own end and through cancel_requested; Cancel mid-chunk; an unconfirmed group end turning Cancel into a failure; an escapee holding its output reported; two ends at once) and the OmniVoice worker (done, an obeyed Cancel and a crash with a helper on /dev/null or on its output; a stubborn worker; an unconfirmed group end never a success or a clean Cancel; an escapee holding its output; under the app window's owner), and qwen3_process.kill_tree's POSIX twins of the Windows tree tests (a child whose parent already exited, the pipe reaching end-of-file) with its identity control. Windows keeps its Job Object and taskkill /T paths and the released worker supervision, pinned by test_kill_tree_keeps_its_windows_paths and test_a_worker_without_a_proved_group_keeps_the_released_supervision, which run everywhere. v0.8.x P5-D-R1 adds 9 more (35): a worker whose identity was not recorded at spawn is never admitted (OmniVoice done and stubborn, the local-engine worker), kill_tree never falls back to signalling a group it cannot prove (running, exited), choosing another engine retires a worker that already exited (with and without a helper), and a Cancel meeting another caller's unconfirmed end is never clean (close, kill). v0.8.x P5-D-R2 adds 7 more (42): a Cancel after another caller fully retired the request's worker unconfirmed is never clean (an answer withheld after close or kill, an escapee holding its output), a worker that died after such a retirement says so, the confirmed control (close, kill), and an end asked for a retired worker answers for it alone. v0.8.x P5-I and P5-I-R3 add 2 more (44) with the same reason text. Nothing Windows ran before is skipped by this rule.

setup.first-run-refuses-a-folder-too-dee.decided: 2026-11-18, the owner's Phase 5 closeout instruction (Decisions.md: P5-G)
setup.first-run-refuses-a-folder-too-dee.why: v0.8.0 P5-G (owner-approved exception): the journey's subject is Windows' own installation-path limit. Production bootstrap.install_path_problem returns no problem on any system but Windows, so a Mac has no refusal to show, and the journey must not fabricate one. The Windows journey and its behaviour are unchanged and still required on Windows. This exception covers this one scenario only (helpers/acceptance_report.DARWIN_NA_SCOPE); every other setup scenario is an automated counterpart. macOS installation, repair and recovery stay with the mandatory fresh-macos qualification (D9b, REAL CLEAN at P7c), which this entry keeps.

setup.first-run-choices-and-cancel.why: v0.8.0 P5-F/P5-F-R1: the macOS counterpart runs the real first-run window (bootstrap.run_with_gui, journeys/setup.py first_run_cancel_macos, adapters/macos/setup_launcher.py) on a disposable copy and the app's own base Python, held first to an isolation preflight computed by the copy's own code (helpers/first_run_journey.py: nothing is launched unless the copy's root, every folder setup writes and its interpreter are right and the copy holds no link) and judged on: exactly Kokoro (ticked, up to 344.7 MB) then OmniVoice (unticked, up to 3.5 GB) with the licensing text and no other engine; all four checkbox states exercised and restored by Tk press and release events; every label given the room its text asks for at 660x600, 700x640, 760x680 and 900x700; Cancel before Begin Setup with exit status 2; no child, folder, launch, connection or install; nothing left running; the copy byte-identical; a bystander installation and the real checkout unchanged. Its evidence is journey checks and real pictures; dialog-contract is not named because Cancel before Begin Setup answers no file or folder dialog. The first native run FAILED on a real clipped licence line (bootstrap wrap margin 48), which was corrected in production (62) before this entry passed. A real base installation stays with fresh-macos.

acceptance.darwin_about: v0.8.x P1B (plan 14.3, MAC-045, D9), revised by the owner's P1B closeout instruction of 2026-11-15: every required scenario and the optional one, exactly one class each. automated: the same journey run by the in-process macOS driver (adapters/macos: real panels, real media, real FFmpeg, acts through Tk, file and message dialogs answered by in-process stand-ins that record the options the application gave them), judged on the evidence its 'evidence' list names (helpers/acceptance_report.DARWIN_EVIDENCE: journey-checks, real-screenshots -- the window server's picture of the application's own window at this run's SHA, PASS on helpers/visual_review.py -- and dialog-contract). No owner signature stands in for an automated check. The real NSOpenPanel and NSAlert are the darwin scenario macos-native-dialogs; what no automation can reach without a privacy grant is listed in darwin_p1b as BLOCKED with the grant it needs. pending_phase: mapped but not yet runnable on macOS, reported NOT RUN until that phase. not-applicable: only a test of the Windows input harness itself (reason windows-input-harness, control.* only), or the one journey whose subject is Windows' own installation-path limit (reason windows-only-installation-path-limit, setup.first-run-refuses-a-folder-too-deep only, keeping fresh-macos; owner P5-G exception 2026-11-18), each with an owner-reviewed reason id (helpers/acceptance_report.DARWIN_NA_SCOPE). A darwin acceptance stage fails on an unmapped scenario, a failed automated counterpart, missing or failed evidence, or a NOT RUN required scenario; it is never a blanket NOT APPLICABLE.

fresh-macos.phase: P1B (contract and procedure); P6a rehearsal; P7c REAL CLEAN
fresh-macos.detail: The packaged archive extracted fresh (quarantined, as a download is), stage 0, the first run, all six tools opened, the .venv damaged and repaired, the app relaunched, an install interrupted and recovered. Mandatory (D9b); its automation is optional. Without a runner it is satisfied only by the owner's run of the written procedure with signed evidence naming the candidate SHA, and its verdict carries its evidence class: SIMULATED, P6a rehearsal or REAL CLEAN (P7c needs REAL CLEAN). A missing run is NOT RUN and blocks publication.

macos-native-dialogs.detail: The real NSOpenPanel and NSAlert, opened by the five tools' own controls in an isolated instance (no stand-ins): each panel's configuration read from the panel itself (title, message, file types, multiple selection, files or folders, starting folder) and held to the tool's contract; each open panel ended through its own cancel: action (what its Cancel button does) and the tool shown to add nothing; each alert pictured and answered with Return and Escape key events posted to the application's own queue, and the application shown to act on the default and do nothing on Escape. Synthetic events, not HID devices: no Accessibility grant is used or claimed. The panel's browser is drawn by another process, so choosing files inside it is not exercised here (darwin_p1b: native-panel-selection).

macos-visual.detail: Pictures of the real application, by the window server, of its own window only (no Screen Recording grant is needed for that): the shell and all six panels in Light and Dark at the 1120 x 800 Aqua minimum and at the largest size the visible desktop holds; empty, populated with long file names and long titles, busy and finished states; a long scrolling list; Preferences; real alerts; output publication and status lines. Each picture carries its tool, appearance, size, state and source SHA, is reviewed by helpers/visual_review.py (decodes, real size, not blank, the appearance asked for, Tk's solid points in place, and Tk's audit: no clipped control, no control outside the window, no overlapping controls, no text under 3.0 contrast), and is indexed in a contact sheet. A missing or unreviewable picture fails. The pictures stay in this run's ignored folder.

macos-kx10.detail: KX-10's behavioural contract, automated: a disposable ACT instance finishes one M4B Maker book, then starts a second real, bounded build; once its FFmpeg encode is seen running (the spawn record and the kernel), that exact application process -- by pid and kernel start time -- is ended with SIGKILL, which is what Force Quit does to a process (no handler, no atexit). Every ACT-owned encoder must be gone within 5 s, no M4B may appear under a final name, the first book must be byte-identical, and a relaunch on the same data must start cleanly and report or recover the staging it finds. The Force Quit window itself (the menu, choosing the app) is not exercised.

Statuses: AUTOMATED PASS, AUTOMATED FAIL, BLOCKED, OWNER VISUAL ACCEPTANCE, APPROVED P1B EXCEPTION (an owner-approved exception: the behaviour stays UNVERIFIED, is never a pass, and relaxes no other requirement), NOT RUN -- LATER PHASE, NOT APPLICABLE -- JUSTIFIED, plus NEEDS RERUN and NOT RUN for evidence a change invalidated or that never ran, and NEEDS RE-REVIEW when application code changed after the owner's visual look. A requirement with no evidence is never a pass.
